files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+Fix a TSAN-reported data race and potential use-after-free when shutting down a subinterpreter with running daemon threads in free-threaded (NOGIL) builds.

review_comments.body: I don't think we want the `_` prefix; this is already a private API. Also, this should be added to the end of the struct, not the beginning.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+Fix a TSAN-reported data race and potential use-after-free when shutting
+down a subinterpreter with running daemon threads in free-threaded (NOGIL)
+builds. The interpreter state could be freed while daemon threads still
+accessed tstate->interp (e.g. during time.sleep). PyInterpreterState now
+keeps an atomic owner refcount and is only finalized/freed when the last
+PyThreadState is destroyed. This fixes
+test_threading.test_daemon_threads_fatal_error.
review_comments.body: This is really long for a news entry. I think having only the first sentence is fine, since users don't understand or care about technical details when reading the changelog.

The convention in this file is to omit a `_` prefix for static functions. Also, this isn't really "finalizing" the interpreter -- finalization is really expensive (think `Py_EndInterpreter` or `Py_Finalize`), while freeing the interpreter is not. Let's call this something else.
It's fine to keep these in `PyInterpreterState_Delete`. We only care about the interpreter structure being valid.
This is a misuse of the `finalizing` field. `finalizing` should be set when we're cleaning up Python-level state, which has already happened.
